blogs.title: Why Attention is the Bottleneck – and How FlashAttention‑3 Breaks It
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains the quadratic scaling problem of self‑attention in Transformers, why it matters for long‑context models, and how FlashAttention‑3’s new hardware‑aware tricks (asynchrony, warp‑specialization, and FP8 support) dramatically speed up the core operation on modern GPUs.

blogs.title: Asynchronous GPU Magic: Producer‑Consumer Warp‑Specialization in FlashAttention‑3
blogs.description: A deep dive into the first technical innovation of FlashAttention‑3. The blog explains the concept of separating producer and consumer warps, how circular shared‑memory buffers and TMA loads work, and why this pipeline hides memory latency to achieve up to 75 % tensor‑core utilization on H100.

blogs.title: Overlapping Softmax with GEMM – The Ping‑Pong Scheduler that Gets More Out of Tensor Cores
blogs.description: Shows how FlashAttention‑3 interleaves the low‑throughput softmax computation with high‑throughput block‑wise GEMMs. The post walks through the 2‑stage (and briefly the 3‑stage) pipelining algorithm, using simple diagrams to illustrate the “ping‑pong” scheduling that pushes performance from 570 TFLOPs to over 640 TFLOPs.

blogs.title: FP8 on Hopper: Turning Low Precision into High Performance Attention
blogs.description: Explains the move from FP16 to FP8 Tensor Cores, including layout constraints, in‑kernel transposes, and register permutations. The article also covers accuracy tricks—block quantization and incoherent processing—that keep numerical error low despite the aggressive 4‑bit exponent format.

blogs.title: From Theory to Numbers: Benchmarks, Ablations, and Accuracy Checks for FlashAttention‑3
blogs.description: Summarizes the empirical results: speedups versus FlashAttention‑2, cuDNN, and PyTorch; ablation study showing each contribution’s impact; and RMSE analysis that demonstrates 2.6× better FP8 accuracy. The post puts the numbers into context for practitioners planning large‑scale inference or training.
